title: P4RPC: First public release
description:
This is a dissector for the Perforce P4RPC wire protocol.h;
it dissects P4RPC over TCP packets, and if the appropriate TLS session
keys are provided then it also dissects P4RPC over TLS.
Add "-v ssl.keylog.file=filename" to your p4 (or p4d, etc) command-line
to save the transient keys into "filename".

This is also plugin-specific code that should have been removed. With ASAN, it will cause a odr-violation complaint.
This is guaranteed to be valid UTF-8.

This is *not* guaranteed to be valid UTF-8, because Unicode code points can be encoded into more than one byte in UTF-8, so a character can be truncated when using a fixed size buffer, and an incomplete character is not valid UTF-8.

Using this buffer, as below, with `proto_item_set_text` and `proto_tree_add_bytes_format`, can create UTF-8 validity errors:

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/20916

There are some routines in `wsutil` for making a string into valid UTF-8; if you know that you have a string which is valid UTF-8 except maybe the last character is truncated, there are somewhat faster things you can do. See the `mark_truncated` function in `epan/proto.c` for an example.

What do you want it to look like when truncated?
